title: CinderPath: A Slay The Spire meets Balatro card game for Android
author: Pelonarax
selftext:
I just published in closed testing my first game. I'm an experienced software dev working in a corporate so I have a really good understanding of software development lifecycle so i want to share with you the approach i took. 

  
First of all meet the team:

\- 20$ Claude  
\- 20$ Codex  
\- 12$ PixelLab   
\- Free Notion Space

I decided to make the game in the first week of September, I had a strong idea of how the game will look like when finished so the goal was pretty well set from the beginning and this helped a lot. 

It took me both Claude and Codex monthly limit and 98% of Pixelab quota. Honestly, not every token was spent against the game but more to create a sustainable workflow and this is how it ended:

Claude Opus is the software architect, it made the plan of every single feature, Claude Sonnet + GPT Terra are the developers working on it and use the Pixelab MCP to create the art needed and place it in game. 

Notion worked as a common knowledge for me and them, I put there task for them and they did for me (human testing, feeling), we also worked on the list of cards and their graphic rapresentation there, so every card is in a Notion database with a description data and art detail. 

  
The cherry on top? I scheduled Sonnet to work at night and do as many run it can to balance the game and give me a report of every possible combination of cards, resulting in auto balancing of the game every time we added feature. 

  
As last step, sonnet managed the release and the creation of the store screenshots and store page optimized for ASO. 

The result? The game is a little rough on the edge but I finally managed to release a full game and i learned a lot with this workflow and I'm ready to do more in less time and with a managed workflow.

If you want to test i put the instructions in comments

comments.author: qing-turn
comments.body: Love the "meet the team" breakdown with prices. Similar background here: programmer by day, first game. I agree that having a clear picture of the finished game from day one helps a lot, the AI moves fast but it needs someone holding the direction. How did you split the work between Claude and Codex?

replies.author: Pelonarax
replies.body:
Another TF2 fan here? 

Honestly? I didn't, I just keep an eye on the 5hours limit. The only clear separation is that Opus has to be the solution architect, so basically he needs to come up with a plan and tell me what work needs to be done and if something is possible doing in parallel, in that case I give the plan to sonnet or terra or both. Sonnet and Terra are basically the same skill level so you don't need to be too picky about it

replies.author: qing-turn
replies.body: Haha, not sure where the TF2 came from, but I'll take it. Opus as the architect who plans and decides what can run in parallel is pretty much our setup too: one session plans and splits the tasks, the others pick them up.
